timeline.changes: Initial schema. Creates public.profiles (id PK ref auth.users ON DELETE CASCADE, email, name, college, gender, created_at, updated_at) with RLS + policies (view all, insert own, update own). Creates public.journeys (user_id, user_email, user_name, train_number, travel_date, coach, boarding/destination_station, college, gender) with RLS (view all, create/update/delete own). Creates public.requests (from_user_id, from_email, from_name, to_user_id, to_email, to_name, train_number, travel_date, stations, status enum pending/accepted/rejected) with RLS. Creates public.conversations (participants uuid[], participant_names jsonb, train_number, travel_date, last_message, last_message_time) with RLS (participant-based). Creates public.messages (conversation_id FK CASCADE, sender_id, sender_name, text, created_at) with RLS using new SECURITY DEFINER function public.is_conversation_participant(conv_id). Creates public.last_read (user_id, conversation_id, timestamp, UNIQUE(user_id,conversation_id)) with RLS. Creates public.update_updated_at_column() trigger function + triggers on profiles and requests. Creates public.handle_new_user() trigger function + on_auth_user_created trigger on auth.users (auto-creates profile row with id+email). ALTER PUBLICATION supabase_realtime ADD TABLE public.messages. Indexes: journeys(user_id), journeys(train_number,travel_date), requests(from_user_id), requests(to_user_id), requests(status), messages(conversation_id), conversations GIN(participants).
Recreates public.update_updated_at_column() adding SET search_path = public (fixes security definer / mutable search_path warning). No other changes.

Drops permissive journeys policy 'Users can view all journeys'. Adds SECURITY DEFINER public.can_view_journey(train_number text, travel_date date) (true if caller has a journey on same train+date). Replaces with 'Users can view own journeys or matching journeys' policy (own OR can_view_journey).

Adds conversations.deleted_for uuid[] DEFAULT '{}' (per-user soft delete). Creates blocked_users (blocker_id, blocked_id, UNIQUE pair) + RLS policies (view/insert/delete own blocks). Creates user_reports (reporter_id, reported_id, reason) + RLS policies (create/view own). Adds SECURITY DEFINER public.is_blocked(a,b) (either direction). Rewrites conversations SELECT policy to exclude rows where caller is in deleted_for. Re-creates conversations UPDATE policy. ALTER PUBLICATION supabase_realtime ADD TABLE public.conversations (presence tracking).

Drops profiles policy 'Users can view all profiles'. Adds SECURITY DEFINER public.can_view_profile(profile_id) (own profile, OR shared train+date journey, OR accepted request, OR shared conversation). Replaces with 'Users can view contextual profiles' SELECT policy. Adds indexes idx_journeys_train_date (IF NOT EXISTS) and idx_requests_status_users(status, from_user_id, to_user_id).

Creates public.trains (train_number PK, train_name, active, created_at) with RLS + 'Anyone can view trains' SELECT policy. Creates public.unverified_trains (train_number, train_name, submitted_by FK auth.users) with RLS (insert own, view own). Adds journeys.train_name column (IF NOT EXISTS). Large bulk INSERT (~200 rows) of popular Indian train data (Rajdhani, Shatabdi, Duronto, Garib Rath, Vande Bharat, Tejas, etc.) with ON CONFLICT (train_number) DO NOTHING.
Adds unverified_trains.entered_value text and normalized_value text columns (IF NOT EXISTS).
Adds 'Users can delete their pending outgoing requests' DELETE policy on requests (auth.uid() = from_user_id AND status = 'pending') - enables cancel.
Drops and re-creates conversations UPDATE policy 'Users can update conversations they participate in' adding WITH CHECK (auth.uid() = ANY(participants)).
Drops and re-creates the same conversations UPDATE policy again with proper USING + WITH CHECK (allows participants to update, including adding themselves to deleted_for).
Creates SECURITY DEFINER public.soft_delete_conversation(conv_id, user_id_to_add) that appends a user to deleted_for, only if the user is a participant and not already present (bypasses RLS).

Adds profiles.bio, hobbies, avatar_url columns. Creates storage bucket 'avatars' (public=true) via INSERT INTO storage.buckets ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. Creates storage.objects policies: 'Users can upload their own avatar' (INSERT, folder = uid), 'Users can update their own avatar' (UPDATE), 'Users can delete their own avatar' (DELETE), 'Avatars are publicly accessible' (SELECT to public).

Adds profiles DELETE policy 'Users can delete own profile'. Integrates is_blocked() into RLS: rewrites journeys SELECT policy (matching-journey arm must NOT be blocked), requests INSERT policy (cannot create request to blocked user), requests SELECT policy (hides requests involving blocked), and can_view_profile() function (adds NOT is_blocked gate). Adds index blocked_users(blocker_id, blocked_id). Sets avatars bucket public=false; drops 'Avatars are publicly accessible'; creates 'Authenticated users can view avatars' SELECT (authenticated only). Adds check constraints on journeys (user_name<=100, train_number<=20, coach<=50, stations<=200, college<=200) and profiles (name<=100, bio<=500, hobbies<=200, college<=200).

Reverts avatars bucket to public=true. Drops storage policies (incl. nonexistent 'Users can view avatars'). Recreates 'Avatars are publicly accessible' SELECT and 'Users can upload/update/delete their own avatar' policies (public read, authenticated upload/update/delete).

UPDATE public.journeys SET user_email = NULL (clears existing emails to prevent exposure). Creates security_invoker view public.profiles_safe that NULLs email unless auth.uid() = id. GRANT SELECT on profiles_safe to authenticated.

Sets avatars bucket public=false again. Drops 'Avatars are publicly accessible' and 'Authenticated users can view avatars' policies. Creates new 'Authenticated users can view avatars' SELECT policy (authenticated only, no anonymous, no public listing).

Drops journeys.user_email column (email leak via can_view_journey). Adds RLS channel authorization on realtime.messages: SELECT policy 'Authenticated users can receive their conversation messages' using realtime.topic() - allows messages-% topics (if participant) and conversations-updates global topic. NOTE: 'ALTER TABLE realtime.messages ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY' line is commented out (relies on managed-Supabase default).

Adds messages.attachment_url, attachment_type, attachment_name, attachment_size columns (IF NOT EXISTS). Adds storage.objects policies for 'chat-attachments' bucket: 'Participants can read chat attachments' (SELECT, is_conversation_participant on first path segment), 'Participants can upload chat attachments' (INSERT, + owner=uid), 'Owners can delete their chat attachments' (DELETE, owner=uid). NOTE: the chat-attachments bucket itself is NOT created in any migration.
ALTER TABLE public.last_read REPLICA IDENTITY FULL. Conditionally adds last_read to supabase_realtime publication (checks pg_publication_tables first).

Large hardening migration. (1) Creates public.prevent_conversation_tamper() trigger function (raises if participants/participant_names/train_number/travel_date/created_at/id change) + trigger conversations_prevent_tamper. (2) Adds SECURITY DEFINER public.is_blocked_in_conversation(conv_id, uid). (3) Adds SECURITY DEFINER public.can_create_conversation(parts uuid[]) (2 participants, caller is participant, not blocked, accepted request exists). (4) Replaces conversations INSERT policy with 'Users can create accepted-companion conversations' (can_create_conversation). (5) Rewrites messages INSERT policy adding NOT is_blocked_in_conversation. (6) Rewrites realtime.messages SELECT policy: adds last-read-% (any auth user) and conversations-updates-<uid> topics. (7) Adds 'Owners can update their chat attachments' storage UPDATE policy. (8) REVOKE EXECUTE on is_conversation_participant, is_blocked, can_view_journey, can_view_profile, soft_delete_conversation, is_blocked_in_conversation, can_create_conversation from anon/public; GRANT EXECUTE to authenticated.

Defense-in-depth: REVOKE UPDATE on public.conversations from authenticated and anon; GRANT UPDATE (last_message, last_message_time, deleted_for) only to authenticated; GRANT ALL on conversations to service_role.

Deletes exploit seed conversation id '11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111'. Rewrites realtime.messages SELECT policy: last-read-% topic now requires is_conversation_participant(substring(topic from 11 for 36)::uuid) instead of open access. messages-% and conversations-updates-<uid> branches kept.

Large security migration. (1) REVOKE SELECT(email) on profiles from authenticated and anon. (2) Adds SECURITY DEFINER public.users_share_journey(a,b,train,tdate); rewrites requests INSERT policy to require shared journey + from_user_id<>to_user_id + not blocked. (3) Replaces can_create_conversation with 3-arg version (parts, train, tdate) matching train/date to accepted request; drops old 1-arg function. (4) Reworks soft_delete_conversation() to enforce self-only (user_id_to_add must equal auth.uid(), raises otherwise) and sets session flag app.allow_deleted_for_update='on'. (5) Reworks prevent_conversation_tamper() to also raise on deleted_for changes unless session flag is set; drops/recreates trigger as prevent_conversation_tamper_trg (NOTE: old trigger conversations_prevent_tamper is never dropped). (6) Adds @graphql({"visible": false}) comments on profiles, conversations, messages, requests, journeys, blocked_users, last_read, user_reports, unverified_trains (hides from pg_graphql; trains stays visible).

Drops 'Authenticated users can view avatars' storage SELECT policy. Creates 'Users can view contextual avatars' SELECT policy: bucket avatars AND (folder uid = own uid OR can_view_profile(folder uid::uuid)) - only contextual users see avatars.

REVOKE SELECT on profiles, profiles_safe, conversations, messages, journeys, requests, blocked_users, last_read, user_reports, unverified_trains FROM anon. REVOKE INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE on blocked_users, unverified_trains, user_reports, conversations, requests, profiles FROM anon.

Re-applies @graphql({"visible": false}) comments to the same 9 tables + profiles_safe view + 7 helper functions (can_create_conversation(uuid[],text,date), can_view_journey, can_view_profile, is_blocked, is_blocked_in_conversation, is_conversation_participant, users_share_journey).
REVOKE EXECUTE on graphql_public.graphql(text,text,jsonb,jsonb) from anon, authenticated, PUBLIC. REVOKE USAGE ON SCHEMA graphql_public from anon, authenticated. (Disables client GraphQL access.)
Re-issues ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY on all 9 tables + re-applies all @graphql visible:false comments (to force pg_graphql schema rebuild). No functional change to RLS.
DROP EXTENSION IF EXISTS pg_graphql CASCADE - removes GraphQL entirely from the project.
REVOKE EXECUTE ON public.handle_new_user() FROM PUBLIC, anon (restricts the auth.user trigger function; trigger still runs as owner).

Final broad grant to authenticated: GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public; GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public; GRANT USAGE, SELECT ON ALL SEQUENCES IN SCHEMA public. (Re-opens table-level UPDATE on all tables incl. conversations, superseding the earlier column-level restriction; also grants on views like profiles_safe.)

finalState: Public schema: 10 tables - profiles, journeys, requests, conversations, messages, last_read, blocked_users, user_reports, trains (verified catalog), unverified_trains - plus view profiles_safe (security_invoker, email shown only to owner). RLS enabled on every table. Profiles/journeys/requests/conversations/messages/last_read all reference auth.users via FKs and all enforce participant/owner/context-based policies; blocked_users and user_reports are owner-scoped. SECURITY DEFINER helpers: is_conversation_participant(uuid), can_view_journey(text,date), can_view_profile(uuid), is_blocked(uuid,uuid), is_blocked_in_conversation(uuid,uuid), can_create_conversation(uuid[],text,date), users_share_journey(uuid,uuid,text,date), soft_delete_conversation(uuid,uuid), update_updated_at_column(), handle_new_user(). Triggers: on_auth_user_created on auth.users (auto-creates profile), update_profiles_updated_at, update_requests_updated_at, and two conversations tamper-guard triggers (conversations_prevent_tamper from 20260630113712 plus prevent_conversation_tamper_trg from 20260703100726, both calling prevent_conversation_tamper()). Conversation UPDATE is functionally restricted: protected columns (participants, participant_names, train_number, travel_date, created_at, id) are blocked by trigger, deleted_for only via soft_delete_conversation() RPC using session flag app.allow_deleted_for_update; last_message/last_message_time/deleted_for were the only column-level grants but the final 20260725073436 grant re-grants full table-level UPDATE to authenticated (trigger remains the real guard). PostgREST grants: anon fully revoked from all core tables (SELECT + DML); authenticated granted SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on ALL TABLES via final grant migration. pg_graphql extension is DROPPED (20260717045003); @graphql visible:false comments remain but are moot. Realtime: supabase_realtime publication includes messages, conversations, last_read; REPLICA IDENTITY FULL only on last_read; realtime.messages has a channel-authorization SELECT policy for authenticated users keyed on realtime.topic() (messages-<convId>, last-read-<convId>-<uid>, conversations-updates-<uid>). Storage buckets: 'avatars' (private, final public=false; SELECT 'Users can view contextual avatars' = own or can_view_profile, plus owner INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policies) and 'chat-attachments' (referenced by participant-based INSERT/SELECT/UPDATE/DELETE policies, but bucket creation is NOT in any migration). journeys.user_email was dropped; email column on profiles is SELECT-revoked; email only accessible via profiles_safe to owner or auth.users. Trains catalog is seeded with ~200 rows and readable by all authenticated users.
authSchemaDetails: All profiles/requests/conversations/messages/last_read/journeys have id/user_id/sender_id/etc. columns that are FKs to auth.users(id) with ON DELETE CASCADE. The initial migration (20251212061640) creates SECURITY DEFINER public.handle_new_user() and an AFTER INSERT trigger on auth.users named on_auth_user_created that inserts a profiles row (id, email only - name/college/gender/bio are not auto-populated, they remain NULL until user updates). 20260722181045 revokes EXECUTE on handle_new_user() from PUBLIC and anon (the trigger still executes because it runs as the function owner). Email handling: profiles.email column has had SELECT revoked from authenticated and anon (20260703100726); the owner can see their own email only via the security_invoker view profiles_safe (20260119144831), or it remains on auth.users.email. There is no email-confirmation logic, no auth.identities references, and no auth admin/RPC code anywhere in migrations; profile auto-creation is the only auth-schema coupling. No changes to auth.email_templates, confirmations, or OAuth config (those live outside SQL migrations in Supabase config, not in these files).
realtimeDetails: supabase_realtime publication membership: public.messages added in 20251212061640 (unconditional ALTER PUBLICATION); public.conversations added in 20251215070131 (for presence); public.last_read added in 20260618111636 (guarded by a pg_publication_tables existence check, so it is the only idempotent one). REPLICA IDENTITY FULL is set only on public.last_read (20260618111636); messages and conversations keep the default (PK-only) identity, so postgres_changes UPDATE events on them will not carry full row payloads. Channel authorization: a SELECT RLS policy on realtime.messages named 'Authenticated users can receive their conversation messages' was introduced in 20260418104404 and rewritten twice (20260630113712, 20260702121413). Final form grants SELECT to authenticated when realtime.topic() is 'messages-'<conversationId> (must be is_conversation_participant), 'last-read-'<conversationId>-<otherUserId> (must be is_conversation_participant of the embedded uuid via substring(topic from 11 for 36)), or 'conversations-updates-'||auth.uid() (per-user broadcast channel). IMPORTANT GOTCHA: the enabling statement 'ALTER TABLE realtime.messages ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY' is commented out in 20260418104404 - enforcement relies on Supabase managed hosting enabling RLS on realtime.messages by default (Realtime v2 channel authorization). The policy uses Supabase-specific realtime.topic() and the realtime schema, i.e. it depends on the Go Realtime server doing channel authorization against realtime.messages RLS. The client topic contract (messages-<uuid>, last-read-<uuid>-<uuid>, conversations-updates-<uid>) is implicit in these policies. An early revision of the last-read-% branch allowed any authenticated user to subscribe to any last-read topic (20260630113712); it was tightened to require conversation participation in 20260702121413.
storageDetails: 'avatars' bucket is created in 20251227101646 via INSERT INTO storage.buckets (id, name, public) VALUES ('avatars','avatars',true) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. Its public flag flip-flopped: true (20251227101646) -> false (20260106151017) -> true (20260106164620) -> false (20260418102918). Final state: public=false (private). Final avatars storage.objects policies: SELECT 'Users can view contextual avatars' (authenticated, bucket avatars AND folder uid == own uid OR can_view_profile(folder uid)) created 20260716172422 (replacing 'Authenticated users can view avatars' and the earlier public one); INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE 'Users can upload/update/delete their own avatar' (authenticated, bucket avatars AND auth.uid()::text = (storage.foldername(name))[1]) last recreated in 20260106164620. Because the bucket is private, avatar files cannot be read by anonymous/URL access and can only be served via authenticated requests or signed URLs. 'chat-attachments' bucket: NO bucket creation statement exists in any migration - only storage.objects policies referencing bucket_id='chat-attachments' (SELECT/INSERT/DELETE in 20260618111613, UPDATE added in 20260630113712), all gated on is_conversation_participant of the first path segment (name format '<conversationId>/<file>') and owner=uid. The bucket itself must have been created out-of-band (dashboard/console) and WILL NOT exist on a fresh self-hosted replay unless created manually. That is a migration completeness gap.
notes: 1) chat-attachments bucket is referenced by storage policies but never created in any migration - a fresh self-hosted replay will have no such bucket; create it manually (INSERT INTO storage.buckets or console). 2) The realtime.messages RLS policy depends on RLS being enabled on realtime.messages, but the ALTER TABLE realtime.messages ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY statement is commented out in 20260418104404; it relies on Supabase managed hosting default. On self-host, verify RLS is enabled on realtime.messages or the channel-authorization policy is inert. 3) Realtime is deeply Supabase-specific: realtime.topic(), the realtime.messages table, and ALTER PUBLICATION supabase_realtime all assume the Supabase Go Realtime server with RLS channel authorization. A self-host must provide that exact Realtime server; a vanilla Postgres logical-replication pubsub will not enforce the channel policies. 4) REPLICA IDENTITY FULL is set only on last_read; messages/conversations keep default identity, so realtime UPDATE events on them will carry only PK columns. 5) pg_graphql is fully dropped (DROP EXTENSION pg_graphql CASCADE, 20260717045003) after several migrations that only worked around it (visible:false comments, ENABLE RLS re-issues to force schema rebuild, REVOKE on graphql_public.graphql). A self-hosted stack that wants GraphQL must re-install and re-secure it. 6) The final broad grant (20260725073436, GRANT ... UPDATE ON ALL TABLES) re-grants table-level UPDATE on conversations to authenticated, technically superseding the column-level restriction from 20260630153027; the prevent_conversation_tamper trigger is what actually still protects conversations.participants/participant_names/train_number/travel_date/created_at/id and deleted_for (deleted_for only writable via soft_delete_conversation() RPC which sets session flag app.allow_deleted_for_update). The same grant also puts INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on the profiles_safe view (harmless at grant time but broad). 7) Duplicate tamper trigger on conversations: 20260630113712 created trigger 'conversations_prevent_tamper'; 20260703100726 created 'prevent_conversation_tamper_trg' and dropped only that new name - the original trigger is never dropped, so BOTH fire on every UPDATE (function is idempotent, so only redundant, not broken). 8) Heavy same-name RLS policy churn across the history (journeys SELECT recreated 3x, conversations UPDATE recreated 4x, requests INSERT/SELECT recreated, realtime.messages SELECT recreated 3x). For a self-host migration only the final definitions matter, but the DROP-before-CREATE pattern must be preserved in order. 9) 20260702121413 deletes an 'exploit seed' conversation (id 11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111), evidence of a past security incident in production - worth auditing before migration. 10) avatars bucket ends private; any client relying on plain public avatar URLs will break - signed URLs or authenticated reads are required. 11) soft_delete_conversation() now hard-requires auth.uid() and self-only; it is SECURITY DEFINER and REVOKEd from anon/public with EXECUTE granted only to authenticated - must keep those grants for the RPC to work. 12) Email is aggressively hidden: journeys.user_email column dropped (20260418104404) after data was NULLed (20260119144831), profiles.email SELECT revoked (20260703100726), owner email only via profiles_safe. Ensure client code does not query profiles.email. 13) The supabase_realtime publication adds for messages/conversations are unconditional; replaying the whole migration set twice would error on 'already a member of publication' for those two (only last_read is guarded). 14) Data-affecting statements exist mid-history (UPDATE journeys SET user_email=NULL; DELETE seed conversation) - they are destructive and will run again on a clean replay (no-op then). 15) The trains seed INSERT (~200 rows) is large and static; unverified_trains.entered_value/normalized_value columns are presumably maintained by app logic, not DB migrations. 16) No auth email-confirmation, identity, or config migrations exist; profile auto-creation is the only coupling to auth, and it depends on the auth.users trigger surviving on self-host.
